convention_family_aggregation.claim: Per-symbol helper candidates of one kind are aggregated into a single family candidate whose matcher is a disjunction over its members and whose coverage is the union of files any member satisfies.
convention_family_aggregation.what_it_is_not: Not a claim that a family member guards, dominates, or cannot be bypassed. Membership is presence-of-a-resolving-call plus, for the auth kind, a syntactic span-containment test that identifies the route's wrapper. No control flow is consulted at inference time.
convention_family_aggregation.false_positive_behavior: A helper exported from the family's own module that is itself a higher-order function wrapping the handler will join the family even if its purpose is unrelated to the kind - a logging or error-handling wrapper living in the auth module is the shape. The wrapper test excludes point-call utilities (measured on dub: hashPassword, hashToken, getSession, validatePassword all excluded) but cannot distinguish two wrappers by intent. No eval repo currently exhibits it; dub's absence of such an export is luck, not design.
convention_family_aggregation.measured: dub auth 0.0324 (best per-symbol) -> 0.5709 (family), members exactly withAdmin/withPartnerProfile/withPublishableKey/withSession/withWorkspace. dub rate limit 0.0385 -> 0.0526, members ratelimit/ratelimitOrThrow. papermark rate limit 0.0813, members checkRateLimit/ratelimit. No family on taxonomy, formbricks, calcom, midday, openstatus. No request-validation family anywhere: dub has zero request_validation_called facts.
convention_family_aggregation.quarantine_status: The three family kinds remain behind --experimental-security. Promotion is blocked and the reason is recorded in docs/beta-run/CV-3-PROMOTION-BLOCKER.md: all three are ENFORCED by control-flow proofs, so they fail the promotion standard requiring presence-only matchers.

presence_only_family_enforcement.claim: Each HANDLER of an accepted convention's routes is checked for a call to one of the accepted members, resolved through its import rather than matched as a string. A route.ts exporting GET and POST is two endpoints and is judged as two.
presence_only_family_enforcement.what_it_is_not: NOT a claim that the route is protected, that the helper runs before anything, or that it cannot be bypassed. The finding wording says so: 'this route does not call any accepted auth wrapper', never 'unprotected' and never 'missing auth'. Promotion is per candidate, not per kind: only a family candidate carrying enforcement_semantics: "presence" is promoted, and the per-symbol candidates of the same kinds remain behind --experimental-security because they are checked by build_auth_boundary_proof, which reasons about control flow.
presence_only_family_enforcement.false_positive_behavior: FALSE NEGATIVES, by construction. Presence asks whether a handler calls an accepted member; it asks nothing about ORDER, REACHABILITY or BRANCHES. So all of these pass: a guard called after the sink it should protect; a guard called only in a catch block or another path that does not run on success; a guard on one side of an if/else while the sink is on the other. Every one of those is a control-flow question, and the tier that answers them is the guard-dominance proof (build_auth_boundary_proof: guard_dominates_straight_line_sinks, branch_bypass_reasons, callback_boundary_reasons), which stays quarantined per docs/architecture/security-heuristic-audit.md. Pinned as a documented non-catch in a_guard_called_after_the_sink_is_a_documented_non_catch, asserted silent rather than left implicit. NOT among the misses, since independent verification found and it was fixed: a route.ts where only one of several exported handlers is wrapped - that is now reported per handler, because judging the file as a whole let 'wrap the read, forget the write' report clean. FALSE POSITIVES: a route that legitimately has no auth - a health check, an OG image endpoint, a public webhook receiver - is reported as calling no wrapper. That is a true statement about the route and not a defect in it, and it is why auth families accept at warn and require an explicit upgrade to block. Resolution covers named imports (including renamed) and namespace imports (`import * as auth` then `auth.withSession`); a helper reached any other way - a deeper property chain, a value passed through a variable - would be reported despite being present. THIRD shape, added by CV-4: presence resolves a call to an accepted SYMBOL NAME via the file's imports and does not compare module specifiers, so a same-named export from an unrelated module satisfies the convention. This is the price of the barrel case - a barrel's specifier is legitimately not the family's module, and deciding by module would need the import-graph chain the presence path deliberately does not consult. Both directions are pinned in crates/drift-engine/tests/presence_enforcement_cv3.rs (a_wrapper_imported_through_a_barrel_satisfies_presence and a_same_named_wrapper_from_an_unrelated_module_also_satisfies_presence), so the trade cannot move silently in either direction.
presence_only_family_enforcement.enforcement_default: warn. An auth family is accepted at warn regardless of coverage; block requires an explicit --mode block from the author. The first intentionally-public route in a repo must not be a false block.
presence_only_family_enforcement.evasion_matrix: CV-4 shapes, all in crates/drift-engine/tests/presence_enforcement_cv3.rs: renamed import satisfies; barrel re-export satisfies; namespace import satisfies; same-named unimported local does NOT; namespace property of an unimported object does NOT; import-only-never-called is reported; a wrong-flavour member is reported with the expected helper named; a test file is not a route and stays silent; per-handler granularity is pinned three ways. Two documented NON-catches are asserted silent: a guard called after the sink it should protect, and the unrelated-module symbol above.

claim_notes.automatic_convention_inference_for_any_d: Candidate inference recognises a data layer only when its import specifier contains prisma, database, db, or data-access (is_data_access_source in crates/drift-engine/src/candidate_command.rs). Repos naming theirs store/supabase/repository/models yield zero inferred candidates. Drift reports this explicitly and suggests the module found by tracing package.json dependencies through repo imports; the human declares it with --data-modules. Claimable capability is therefore 'bootstraps and enforces a declared layering contract with per-line evidence', not 'learns your conventions'. Lift when structural construction-site detection lands.
claim_notes.security_boundary_proofs: The security heuristics layer is gated behind --experimental-security for beta and its conventions are never auto-accepted. Its own audit (docs/architecture/security-heuristic-audit.md) found guard dominance is a line-number comparison, branch detection is line.contains("if"), and unsupported_dynamic_control_flow() - the valve meant to degrade a proof when control flow is too dynamic - matches only Drift fixture strings, so it opens for test inputs and never for real dynamic dispatch. The findings are not worthless but cannot honestly be called proofs. Lift when the layer is rebuilt on AST analysis.

enforcement_posture.note: EW-10. What a reader is actually getting. `enforced` claims can fail a build; `advisory` claims report and leave the decision to a human. The distinction is not cosmetic - a convention in warn mode produces findings and exit 0, and a reader who assumed otherwise would conclude Drift found nothing.
enforcement_posture.single_convention_scope: Enforced by default: api_route_no_direct_data_access, on TypeScript/JavaScript Next.js API routes (App Router and Pages). Advisory by default: the three presence-only family kinds (auth helper, rate limit, request validation), which report at warn until an author upgrades them. The guard-dominance and dataflow versions of those same kinds remain behind --experimental-security and are not claimed at all.

measured_refusal_rate.note: How often Drift declines to answer about an edit that is not a violation. Eight ordinary edits per repo - a comment, a new layered route, a new helper, a helper plus its caller, an added local import, an appended export, two new routes in one diff, and a moved route - none of which breaks the data-access convention. A refusal (exit 3) on any of them is Drift failing to be useful about work it should understand completely. Derived from the harness baseline by scripts/sync-refusal-rate.mjs, never typed by hand.

measured_determinism.note: EW-7 (DET-2). Determinism is the marketed claim, and the published evidence covered taxonomy and papermark - neither of which is where the one observed flap happened. cal.com is, and it had never been measured. A run's digest covers what a user would notice change: exit code, check status, blocking count, partial-coverage flag, parser-gap count, and every finding's fingerprint, enforcement result, file, line and specifier. Ids and durations that vary by invocation by design are excluded, or the digest would differ every run and prove nothing.
measured_determinism.contamination_guard: scripts/worktree-contamination.mjs - a worktree with foreign changes is refused rather than measured, naming every injected file. Before this, 'it was harness contamination' and 'determinism is not what we claim' left identical evidence behind.
measured_determinism.digest_stability_note: A digest is stable across runs of one build, not across builds. cal.com and papermark changed digest when the renamed-re-export fix removed false unresolved-symbol diagnostics from their parser-gap counts, which the digest covers; taxonomy, which has no renamed re-exports, did not. That is the digest working. Comparing a digest against one recorded at a different commit is a category error, which is why the commit is recorded beside it.

enforcement_posture.presence_family_note: presence_only_family_enforcement is advisory because an auth family is accepted at warn by default: it produces findings and exits 0. Block is reachable, but only when the author passes --mode block explicitly, because a repo's first intentionally-public route - a health check, an OG image endpoint, a webhook receiver - would otherwise be a false block. Classing this as enforced would describe a product the reader does not get by default.
